label.purpose: Buttons, nav items, form labels, 500 weight.

display.purpose: Largest headline moments only; 900 is synthetic bold, deliberately.

mono.purpose: Code and tabular/measurement data only — never a costume for 'technical'.

shadows.name: glass-shadow
shadows.purpose: Every glass surface: sidebar, header, dropdown menus, dialogs, the auth card. No exceptions, no variants.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Default interactive transition (button press, sidebar width, slide/scale-in).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, brand-colored action per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #ff7a00; color: #1a1005; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-weight: 500; font-family: Rubik, system-ui, sans-serif; border: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(255,122,0,0.2); transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgb(255 143 41); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,122,0,0.5); }

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: The auth/setup card — the flagship example of the liquid-glass recipe. 28px radius is reserved for this role.
components.css: .ds-glass-card { background: linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(10,10,10,0.5) 0%, rgba(10,10,10,0.6) 55%, rgba(10,10,10,0.54) 100%); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.22); border-radius: 28px; box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.25); backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(160%); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(22px) saturate(160%); padding: 32px; }

components.name: Glass Nav Bar
components.description: The sidebar rail and top header — same recipe as Glass Card at a lighter 18px blur, no radius (flush to the viewport edge).
components.css: .ds-glass-bar { background: linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(10,10,10,0.5) 0%, rgba(10,10,10,0.6) 55%, rgba(10,10,10,0.54) 100%); border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.22); box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.25); backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(160%); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(160%); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Deliberately flat, never glass — legibility for the value being typed outranks ambient chrome.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #141414; border: 1px solid #2e2e2e; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; color: #c1c2c5; font-family: Rubik, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #ff7a00; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,122,0,0.2); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #909296; }

narrative.overview: Review's whole surface reads as a dim screening room: a near-black space where the only warm light is a single tally-signal orange, and every piece of interface chrome is a pane of frosted glass floating a few inches off the wall behind it. This is a direct, brief-pinned reuse of the liquid-glass system already shipped on Review's sibling tool, Transfer — same accent hex, same near-black palette, same glass recipe, same font. The two apps are meant to read as one family.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#050505) with one warm accent, never a second competing hue
Floating chrome is glass (blurred, translucent, bordered); form controls are not
Dark is the only mode — no light/dark toggle in the internal app
28px radius is reserved for true card surfaces; bars and menus stay on the standard scale
Rubik at 300-600, headline weight 900 riding on synthesized bold by design

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Ember Signal is the only saturated color anywhere in the interface. Status colors exist but are used only for their literal semantic meaning.

rules.name: The Text-Inverse Rule
rules.body: Text on an Ember Signal surface is near-black (#1a1005), never white — contrast wins over the reflex to put light text on a colored button.

rules.name: The No-Serif Rule
rules.body: Rubik is the only typeface anywhere in the product UI outside code/data contexts. No system-font fallback ever stands in as the display voice.

rules.name: The Chrome-Not-Content Rule
rules.body: Glass is reserved for app chrome — navigation, floating bars, menus, dialogs, and the auth card. Never buttons, badges, or arbitrary content containers.

rules.name: The Card-Only 28px Rule
rules.body: 28px radius means this is a card, full stop. A menu or dialog rounded to 28px would read as a card and confuse the hierarchy.

dos: Do keep Ember Signal (#ff7a00) as the only saturated color anywhere in the product.
Do reserve the 28px glass radius for actual cards; use the standard scale for bars, menus, and dialogs.
Do keep buttons, inputs, and switches flat and crisp.
Do use near-black (#1a1005), not white, as text on any Ember Signal-filled surface.
Do treat dark as the only mode inside the app; a share link may still offer its own light/dark choice for external viewers.
donts: Don't show freeframe's own logo mark as Review's default identity.
Don't apply the glass recipe to a button, chip, or badge.
Don't add a second saturated color anywhere without revisiting the One Signal Rule first.
Don't reintroduce a user-facing light/dark toggle inside the app's own chrome without a deliberate product decision to reverse the dark-only call.
